title: Silverpine self-serve runway and hosting choice discovery
summary: Introductory discovery with Silverpine to understand constraints for a pilot. They are leaning toward self-serve hosted to move quickly but have regulatory customers that may later require VPC/dedicated. Discussed free credits, expected TTFT, security checklist, and a next technical deep dive to scope a pilot. Agreement to share pricing and security pack; schedule pilot kickoff and provide 30k token credits.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Start: 4:00 PM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (CTO, Silverpine), Maya Chen (Sr ML Eng), Ravi Kapoor (Platform Lead)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on self-serve path, credits, hosting choices, security fit

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Liam: Good thanks, uh yeah excited to understand how fast we can get something running. We're evaluating hosted for speed but worried about data residency for some EU customers.
00:18 Priya: Great, we'll walk through both the self-serve hosted flow and what the dedicated/VPC options look like later. Quick question — what's your primary eval goal? Latency, cost, or quality?
00:28 Maya: Primary is latency and predictable unit cost. We also want to see model parity with our existing open model stack. We do some post-processing so throughput matters.
00:40 Jordan: Got it. Also, are you planning to prototype via our self-serve API and free credits or do you want Redwood Dedicated right away?
00:47 Ravi: Prefer to start self-serve, get to first token quickly. But timeline tight — a pilot for a key customer in eight weeks. If that works we might escalate to dedicated or VPC.
00:58 Priya: That timeline is doable. Self-serve TTFT (time-to-first-token) for engineering teams — we usually see teams hit first successful call within hours; a simple integration can be done same day. For a pilot scaled to production traffic we often suggest a dedicated capacity evaluation 4–8 weeks in.
01:15 Liam: When you say hours, is that with our infra or via Redwood hosted? We prefer hosted to reduce ops burden.
01:22 Jordan: Hosted. With our SDKs and a quickstart sample you can be calling the API in under an hour. We'll give trial credits — typically 10k–50k tokens depending on the pilot scope.
01:32 Maya: Perfect. Two clarifying points: (1) how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching — we do heavy context reuse, and (2) encryption and KMS integration? Sometimes transcripts show 'K-V cash' in notes, heh.
01:44 Priya: For caching, we have automatic KV/prefix caching at the platform level; it's transparent to the API. Sorry if docs say K-V cash, that's a typo you'll see in older notes. For encryption, hosted uses server-side encryption and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we offer key-rotation and encrypted at rest but not customer-managed keys unless you go VPC/private with KMS integration.
02:10 Ravi: Are there SOC2 reports or an ISO attestation we can review? Also SSO — our SREs want SAML/SSO for console access.
02:18 Jordan: Yes, we can share the SOC2 Type II pack and an enterprise security brief. SSO via SAML is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports OAuth and SSO for workspace owners — we'll include exact flow in the security packet.
02:34 Maya: Good. About performance — can you route to different regions? Our EU customer needs inference in eu-west to keep latency low.
02:42 Priya: Yes, region routing is supported. For hosted, we have endpoints in NA and EU; can route by policy. For full residency guarantees we'd recommend Dedicated in the EU region or Private on-prem.
02:55 Liam: Cost question — we care about cost per token. Do you have guidance on batching vs latency tradeoffs?
03:02 Priya: Absolutely. We provide Optimize suggestions: batching windows, continuous batching, and quantization profiles. There's a tradeoff — bigger batches reduce cost but can increase tail latency. For interactive use we tune for small batches and prefix caching which reduces per-token cost for repeated prompts. We'll share a cost model spreadsheet example.
03:24 Jordan: Quick qualification: what's your expected QPS for the pilot and peak?
03:29 Maya: For pilot maybe 3–5 rps at peak, with bursts to 10 for short windows.
03:35 Priya: That is well within self-serve hosted. If you grow beyond sustained 50 rps we'd recommend Dedicated.
03:42 Ravi: On compliance: audit logs and data retention — can hosted be configured to retain logs for 90 days and give us access to raw request logs?
03:50 Jordan: We can configure extended retention as an add-on; hosted gives operational logs and tracing at the route/model level. For detailed raw request logs and longer retention, Dedicated or Private is cleaner for compliance.
04:05 Liam: Ok makes sense. Another practical item — do you support function calling / structured output? We need to call our internal microservices after generation.
04:13 Priya: Yes, function/tool calling is supported; streaming responses and structured JSON outputs too. We have a short sample in the quickstart repo.
04:22 Maya: Nice. Any gotchas with rate-limiting during the trial? We don't want to hit hard limits during the initial load test.
04:28 Jordan: Trial accounts have soft limits — we can pre-configure higher quotas for your trial. We'll coordinate with support.
04:35 Liam: Great. Who else from Redwood will help run benchmarks? We might want an SE-led perf test with our prompt sets.
04:42 Priya: I can run a perf session — we typically bring a small harness, run latency and throughput benchmarks against your prompt sets, including realistic sequence lengths. We'll need a shared prompt file and a small set of sample docs.
04:55 Maya: We'll prepare a prompt set and an evaluation metric doc. Is there a recommended token budget for a useful perf run?
05:02 Priya: For a representative run, 30k–100k tokens depending on sequence lengths. We often provision 50k trial tokens for that.
05:10 Jordan: Okay, quick recap of constraints: (1) pilot in 8 weeks, (2) start on hosted self-serve to hit TTFT quickly, (3) security info required for internal compliance review, (4) a perf deep-dive run with sample prompts, and (5) pricing and quotas for trial.
05:29 Liam: Yep that's right. Any initial blockers on our side?
05:33 Ravi: Our legal team will want to see data processing addendum and EU data flow details, but that's downstream.
05:39 Jordan: We'll include DPA and region residency notes in the security pack.
05:43 Maya: One more tiny detail — what language models are in the catalog? We use a mix of open LLMs quantized to 4-bit for cost— do you have recommendations?
05:54 Priya: We support multiple open models; for cost-sensitive production we recommend quantized variants with a small quality eval. We'll suggest a few: LlamaX-7B-q4, Omega-13B-fp16, and Redwood-verified versions. We'll attach a model recommendations doc.
06:10 Liam: Awesome. Sounds like a plan.
06:13 Jordan: Next steps — I'll send the pricing deck, security pack, and propose a time for an SE perf deep-dive. Priya will coordinate the perf harness and trial token allocation.
06:25 Ravi: Works for us. Let's pencil in a technical deep dive next Wednesday if possible.
06:29 Jordan: I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 2026-06-24 10am PT pending your confirmation.
06:35 Maya: That works. Thanks everybody.
06:37 Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with artifacts.
06:40 [call ends]

Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions: 'K-V cache' was sometimes written 'K-V cash'; some proper names slightly off in auto notes.
